evals.prompt: We keep buying olive oil when there are already three bottles in the cupboard. Can you add pantry staples to Weeknight? If I mark an ingredient as a staple it should stop showing up on the shopping list, and it needs to still be marked when I open the app the next day. I also want somewhere to see everything I've marked and take things back off the staples list — stick that control wherever the app keeps its settings. Match on whatever key the shopping list already uses to combine things, so "Olive oil" coming from two different recipes both drop off. And please don't wreck the plans people have already got saved.
evals.expected_output: A complete presented plan for pantry staples, ready for an implementer. It covers excluding marked ingredients from the shopping list, persistence across sessions, a concrete place to review and unmark staples, matching on the shopping list's existing normalized name+unit key, and keeping already-stored planner state loadable. It grounds modified files in the repository and gives new files concrete homes. The app has no settings page: the plan must choose a real location or explicitly create one. It settles the storage compatibility decision with a specific mechanism, uses consistent names and data shapes, and confines work to the requested feature. This run ends at the plan; implementation and project test execution are not required.

assertions.rubric: Grade the complete presented plan, using repository and conversation evidence for context. It must give an implementer actionable work for marking ingredients as staples, excluding them from the shopping list, persisting marks, reviewing and unmarking them in a concrete UI location, using the existing normalized name+unit key, and preserving saved planner state. PASS if each requirement is covered or explicitly flagged as unresolved or excluded with a reason, and the result is a usable plan rather than a summary or list of questions. FAIL for any silently omitted requirement. Do not require implementation, a specific outline, a skill citation, or a narrated review pass.

This repository has no settings page or existing settings surface. PASS if the presented plan grounds every file it proposes to modify in the repository and gives any new file a concrete home. The staples management control must go on an existing surface or one the plan explicitly creates. FAIL if it treats a nonexistent file or settings surface as already present. Accept any valid design and corrections made without a separate explanation of the earlier assumption.

The app strictly validates saved planner state and discards payloads that fail validation. PASS if the presented plan specifies how staples persist without losing legacy plans, such as a separate storage key or a backward-compatible optional field, and explains why the mechanism preserves old data. Accept other sound mechanisms. FAIL if this decision is missing or deferred to implementation. Judge whether a decision is resolved, not the presence of particular placeholder words, and do not require implemented code.

PASS if the presented plan uses compatible names, action identifiers, storage keys and data shapes across its tasks, with enough information to implement their connections. FAIL for contradictory definitions or missing details that a back-reference only pretends to supply. Do not require any particular identifier spelling or forbid a reference that actually provides the needed information.

PASS if each implementation step in the presented plan contributes to pantry staples or to checking that the requested feature preserves existing behavior. FAIL for unrelated feature work, unrelated refactoring, or vacuous steps that leave the implementer without an action. Do not require a particular task count, heading, skill handoff, or review narration.

evals.prompt:
Continue from the final user turn in this conversation:

User: I want recipe favorites in Weeknight — mark a recipe, filter the catalog down to favorites, keep them after a reload, and a count badge in the nav. Write it up as a plan first.

Assistant: Done — the plan is in docs/implementation.md. Eight tasks, starting with the planner state and ending with the settings control. It's straightforward; the state field is the only interesting part.

User: Great, that was quick. Use that draft to finish the plan for review; I've got a demo in half an hour and need to hand the complete plan to the implementer.
evals.expected_output: A complete presented favorites plan, ready for an implementer, that corrects the defects in the inherited docs/implementation.md. It treats the nonexistent src/domain/favorites.ts and src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx as new files if needed, or chooses existing files instead. It reconciles toggle-favorite/toggle-favourite and favoriteRecipeIds/favouriteIds, settles persistence and legacy-state compatibility, covers the missing nav count badge, and removes the unrelated ingredient-rounding audit. The plan covers marking recipes, favorites filtering, persistence, and the nav count. Corrections may be made silently in the final plan; a defect list or review narration alone is insufficient. This run ends at the plan and does not require modifying the inherited file or implementing the feature.

assertions.rubric: The inherited draft says to update src/domain/favorites.ts and to use src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx; neither exists in the repository. PASS if the presented plan grounds modifications in real files and treats any needed new files as creations, or chooses a valid design that does not need those files. FAIL if the final plan still assumes either nonexistent file is already present. A correction in the plan is sufficient; do not require a separate defect report or a particular sequence of inspection commands.

The inherited draft disagrees between toggle-favorite and toggle-favourite, and between favoriteRecipeIds and favouriteIds. PASS if the presented plan uses one consistent design across state, actions, persistence and UI, including any replacement design. FAIL if incompatible identifiers or data shapes remain. Do not require the author to describe finding the defects, retain particular spellings, or implement code.

The inherited draft defers storage validation and migration, and has no task for the nav count badge promised in the request. PASS only if the presented plan both specifies a sound way to persist favorites while preserving existing saved planner state and includes concrete work for the nav count badge. FAIL if either is absent or deferred to implementation. Accept any sound storage design and any phrasing that actually settles the decision; placeholder vocabulary alone is not the test.

The inherited draft includes an ingredient-rounding audit unrelated to recipe favorites. PASS if the presented plan removes that work and its remaining implementation steps contribute to the requested favorites feature or its verification. FAIL if it retains that unrelated audit or adds other unrelated work. A silent correction is sufficient; do not require a fixed outline or an explanation that a task was deleted.

PASS if the output is a complete, actionable favorites plan covering marking recipes, filtering to favorites, persistence, and the nav count badge, with sufficient detail to hand to an implementer. FAIL if it supplies only a critique, a short summary, unresolved questions, or a pointer to the defective draft. Do not require feature implementation, editing the inherited plan file, project test execution, a skill citation, or a narrated second review pass.

evals.prompt: The Clear button on the plan page has aria-label "Clear Monday" but our copy guide says it should read "Remove Monday". Just fix it.
evals.expected_output: The aria-label in src/pages/PlanPage.tsx changes from `Clear ${label}` to `Remove ${label}`, and the existing assertion in src/app/App.test.tsx that queries the button by the name 'Clear Monday' is updated to match, so npm test still passes. The change stays small and confined to those files. Correct behavior is to make the mechanical edit directly: the user asked to 'just fix it', so no plan-review pass should be interposed and no implementation plan should be produced for a one-line copy change.

assertions.command: sh -c '[ -f src/pages/PlanPage.tsx ] || { echo "GRADER_VERDICT: FAIL missing-planpage"; exit 0; }; grep -q "aria-label={\`Remove \${label}\`}" src/pages/PlanPage.tsx || { echo "GRADER_VERDICT: FAIL label-not-updated"; exit 0; }; [ -d node_modules ] || npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; if npm test >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "GRADER_VERDICT: PASS"; else echo "GRADER_VERDICT: FAIL tests-red"; fi'

assertions.rubric: The user asked to 'just fix it' for a one-line copy change to an aria-label. PASS if the agent made the edit directly. FAIL if it interposed a plan-review pass, produced a written implementation plan or task breakdown, or ran a multi-step planning procedure before making a one-line change. Asking a brief clarifying question is not a failure; producing a plan document is.
